fault_operand.name_cross_reference: Core-resident method-definition pointer cross-references to isinstance in the mapped executable. The pointed-to name string is not itself core-backed, so the specific name is a mapped-file cross-reference, not resident string evidence.
fault_operand.supported_conclusion: A function object occupies the evaluator operand position requiring an iterator. Core-backed object/type slots, registers, PC and recovered frames support the invalid iterator operand and NULL tp_iternext call at this instant.
fault_operand.limit: The antecedent corruption or incorrect operand production is unknown. The finding does not establish a JSON, NumPy, compiler, CPython or hardware defect.

executable_text_correction.corrected_earlier_interpretation: The preliminary report incorrectly described fault-site disassembly as resident instruction bytes matching disk. GDB had fallen back to the executable file. Its compare-sections .text MIS-MATCHED output does not demonstrate resident code corruption or an ASLR mismatch: the entire text range is absent from core-backed pages.
executable_text_correction.disk_source_interpretation: The build-matched return site disassembles as mov 8(r15),rax; mov r15,rdi; call *0xe0(rax). This interprets the core-backed register/type/NULL-slot facts but is not an attestation of resident instruction bytes.

No causal conclusion or load-related exclusion is supported.
